chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Ayub ibn Nuh from Safwan ibn Yahya from Musa ibn Bakr from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'Some of your freed slaves married into a family, and the women claimed that there was breastfeeding (kinship) between them.' He said, 'As for one, two, or three feedings, it is of no consequence, unless the nurse is a hired woman who resides with him.'

This report explicitly indicates that the intended meaning for the negation of prohibition is one, two, and three feedings, and not more than that, because the specific amount that causes prohibition was not mentioned at all.
ai.seo_question: Does breastfeeding for only one or two times create a permanent marriage prohibition in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that one to three feedings do not establish a permanent mahram relationship unless the nurse is a hired woman residing with the child, a nuance highlighted by the absence of mention regarding the five-feedings threshold in this specific narration. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that while five feedings are the standard for prohibition, specific conditions like the nurse's residency can validate lesser amounts, whereas casual minor feedings remain insufficient.
